canonical_statement: For every finite dimension n and every C1 real function f for which f squared, f squared log(f squared), and the squared norm of its Frechet derivative are integrable under the centered product Gaussian of coordinate variance one, the entropy of f squared is at most twice its Gaussian Dirichlet energy.
domain_and_universes: n : Nat; f : (Fin n -> Real) -> Real; Prop in universe 0; product of n copies of gaussianReal 0 1
hypotheses: Integrable (fun x => norm (fderiv Real f x) ^ 2) (standardGaussian n)
conclusion: entropySquare f (standardGaussian n) <= 2 * integral (fun x => norm (fderiv Real f x) ^ 2) (standardGaussian n)

encoding_decisions.gaussian_measure: Measure.pi of gaussianReal 0 1 over Fin n; this fixes centered identity covariance
encoding_decisions.entropy: integral xlogx(f^2) minus m log m, m = integral f^2; xlogx 0 is definitionally zero
encoding_decisions.energy: integral of the squared operator norm of fderiv Real f
encoding_decisions.regularity: ContDiff Real 1 plus explicit integrability of all three displayed integrands
